title: Appeal to martyrs refuted
english: So when they have been refuted on all these points and find themselves at a loss, they try to take refuge in the martyrs. They say they have many martyrs, and that this is trustworthy proof of the power of the spirit they call prophetic. But this, as it seems, is anything but true. For some of the other heresies also have a great many martyrs, and surely we shall not assent because of this, nor shall we confess that they possess the truth. First of all, those from the heresy of Marcion, called Marcionites, say they have a great many martyrs of Christ, yet they do not confess Christ himself according to truth.
And after a little the same author adds to this, saying:

Therefore, whenever those called to martyrdom for the faith according to truth from the church happen to be together with some of the so-called martyrs from the heresy of the Phrygians, they are at variance with them, and they are perfected without having had communion with them, because they do not wish to assent to the spirit through Montanus and the women. And that this is true, and that it happened in our own times at Apamea on the Maeander in the case of Gaius and Alexander from Eumeneia, who bore witness, is clear.
orientation: The author has just finished listing the earlier proofs against the Montanists and now turns to their claim that their many martyrs prove the power of their prophetic spirit.

title: The author's source for the Miltiades argument
english: I found these words in a writing of theirs, in which they oppose the writing of Miltiades, a fellow Christian. In that writing Miltiades demonstrates that a prophet must not speak in ecstasy. I excerpted these words from it.
orientation: The author is explaining where he found the argument he has just quoted, namely in a writing of theirs that opposed Miltiades' work.

title: The false prophet's ecstasy and the unprovable succession
english: But the false prophet speaks in ecstasy, and with ecstasy come recklessness and fearlessness. He begins with willful ignorance and ends, as I said before, in involuntary madness of soul. They will not be able to show that any prophet of the old covenant or the new was borne by the Spirit in this way. Not Agabus, not Judas, not Silas, not Philip's daughters, not Ammia in Philadelphia, not Quadratus. Nor will they boast of any others who have nothing to do with them.
Then a little later the same author says this:

"For if, as they claim, the women around Montanus succeeded to the prophetic spiritual gift after Quadratus and Ammia in Philadelphia, let them show who among them succeeded to those from Montanus and the women. The apostle insists that the prophetic spiritual gift must remain in the whole church until the final coming. But they could not show anyone, this being already the fourteenth year, I suppose, since Maximilla's death."
orientation: The author is quoting from a Montanist writing against Miltiades, then continues his own argument that no genuine prophet, old or new, can be shown to have prophesied in ecstasy, and that the Montanists cannot show successors to Montanus and the women.
